html:
The Scythians were Iranian-speaking horse nomads who dominated the steppe north of the Black Sea from about 700 BCE. The chart's Scythians and Saka bar covers them with their eastern cousins.

They came west from Central Asia in the 800s and 700s BCE and pushed out the Cimmerians. In the 600s BCE they rode through the Caucasus and raided West Asia until the Medes drove them back. They fought as mounted archers. Around 513 BCE Darius the Great marched a Persian army across the Danube after them; they retreated, burned the grass and wore him down.

Herodotus describes them at length: kings buried with horses and servants under great mounds, the use of hemp smoke, farming Scythians who grew grain for sale to the Greek colonies on the coast. Their gold work, often made by Greek craftsmen, is famous.

From the 200s BCE the Sarmatians took over the steppe. Scythians held on in Crimea, beside the Bosporan Kingdom, until the Goths overwhelmed them in the 200s CE.
